description.p: Axiotask is a fast, local-first frontend for Google Tasks. It keeps your lists in a local database, so it launches in under two seconds and stays fully usable offline; changes sync back to Google as soon as you are connected again.
Built for people who live in their task list:

ul.li: Smart views — Focus, Upcoming, Missed, Unscheduled — across every list
Complete, schedule and reorder in one gesture: a click or drag on the desktop, a swipe on Android
Subtasks, notes and due dates in a task detail panel
The same app on Linux desktop and Android

description.p: Subtasks in the task detail are now full task rows: they show notes and link badges, an unsynced dot, and the same one-tap date menu the list uses, and on a phone they swipe. Reorder them by dragging — the up/down buttons are gone — with one Undo per drop. Finished subtasks fold under a "N completed" group, and completing or deleting a parent now says how many subtasks went with it.

On the phone the new-task composer now opens at the TOP of the list, pinned under the app bar: each task you add appears immediately below it, the field keeps its focus and its date, and the keyboard can no longer cover it.
Previous/Next in the task detail now step through a subtask's checklist, so a subtask no longer strands the panel's navigation.
First packaged Linux release of the Flutter application.
